Description: The P​​rofessional Master's in Applied Systems Engineering (PMASE) is a comprehensive system engineering program designed to give practicing engineers the mathematical, scientific, and engineering foundation to develop, deploy, and evaluate various modeling and analysis strategies. [2] It is a rigorous graduate degree designed to build deep expertise. [2] PMASE gives engineers an effective blend of business, leadership, and in-depth advanced systems engineering domain knowledge through application-based exercises, labs, case studies and capstone group projects. [2] The degree program's learning outcomes include how to: Develop systems thinking skills that support employing various analytic strategies to develop a holistic perspective of the relationships among systems components and the environment. [2] Develop the capacity to apply modeling and simulation to determine and apply the best modeling and simulation approaches. [2] Apply Model-Based Systems Engineering (MBSE) techniques through system lifecycle. [2] Assess tools and techniques, resources, organizational systems, and decision-making processes for the successful management of projects. ProgramName: Master of Architecture
Description: The M.Arch is a STEM-designated professional practice program of architecture that leads to licensure in architecture. Fully accredited by the National Architectural Accrediting Board (NAAB), this degree option provides flexibility for students who have an undergraduate degree with a major in architecture as well as those with a degree in a field other than architecture. The M.Arch. Program requires a minimum of 60 credit hours and a maximum of 102 credit hours of study, full-time and in-person, depending upon the applicant's prior education in architecture and the amount of advanced standing credit granted upon admission to the program. Please note: Successful completion of the Master of Architecture requires a minimum grade of C in all courses. Advanced standing credit is only granted for courses in which the student received a grade of A or B. Normally, a student admitted to the program with maximum advanced standing can expect to complete the program within two academic years (4 semesters) of full-time study. A student admitted to the program with no advanced standing can expect the program to require three years (7 semesters) or full-time study. Graduates from four-year undergraduate programs in architecture similar to that at Georgia Tech can normally expect to complete the program in two academic years, provided they have pursued architecturally related elective coursework during their undergraduate years.

The astrophysics degree provides comprehensive and rigorous training in the fundamental processes and laws that govern planetary systems, stars, galaxies, and the Universe. In addition to these core topics, the degree includes training in computational techniques and data analysis that can be in applied to a variety of disciplines. The skills learned as part of the B.S. in Astrophysics are transferable to a wide range of careers across multiple sectors of the digital economy, such as data scientists, software engineers, and research analysts. Graduates have found jobs in the finance sector, with Fortune 500 companies, and at innovative start-ups. [3] The minor will cover topics and foster skills that are essential for all scientists, engineers, businesspersons, and policymakers who get involved with projects in impoverished countries. [3]
ScholarshipType: Merit-Based Scholarships, Need-Based Scholarships, Demographic Scholarships, Field of Study Scholarships, Scholarships For Community Service

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in International Affairs

Description: The Bachelor of Science in International Affairs (BS INTA) program includes instruction in international affairs, foreign languages, ethics and philosophy, social and natural sciences, and computer science. Upper-division coursework provides training in four substantive areas: technology, and scientific analysis, and ethics;; international security and diplomacy;; comparative politics, cultures, and societies; and; international political economy. [2] Graduates of the BS INTA program are prepared for advanced graduate and professional study and are ready for employment in internationally oriented firms, government agencies, and nonprofit organizations. [2] International Affairs majors are expected to enhance their education through participation in the International Plan, study abroad programs, internships, and a host of on- and off-campus programs. [2] The Bachelor of Science in International Affairs (INTA) is an interdisciplinary degree program designed to provide students with the skillset they will need to engage in strategic planning and analysis in an interdependent and multicultural world. [3] The INTA curriculum gives students the flexibility to build the program based on their post-graduation plan. [3]
ScholarshipAmount: Scholarship amounts vary. For example, the Georgia Tech Val-Sal Scholarship for eligible Georgia residents is between $2,500 and $5,000 annually. [25] The Stamps President's Scholarship can range from $5,400 to $72,000 annually. [15]
ScholarshipType: Georgia Tech offers merit-based and need-based scholarships. [16] There are also specific programs for Georgia residents like the HOPE and Zell Miller Scholarships. [16] Institutional scholarships are also available, some of which are awarded automatically based on the admission application. [20]

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in International Affairs and Modern Languages

Description: The Bachelor of Science in International Affairs and Modern Languages (IAML) is a joint degree offered by the Sam Nunn School of International Affairs and the School of Modern Languages. [1] The program provides students with intensive foreign language training and the essential quantitative skills needed to succeed in international businesses and organizations. [1] Graduates are equipped with the technical, scientific, language, and international affairs knowledge to interact with other societies and cultures. [1] The curriculum is designed around cultural perspectives, global business, government knowledge, essential humanities skills, and technological innovation, preparing students for graduate and professional studies, as well as employment in internationally oriented firms, government agencies, and nonprofit organizations. [2] A key component of the program is an international experience, which can be fulfilled through a study, research, or internship experience abroad. [1, 4]

ProgramName: International Business, Language, and Culture (Minor)

The minor is comprised of both advanced management courses and advanced courses in a foreign language and is designed to prepare students for global leadership by equipping students with the fundamentals of business and the ability to communicate across different languages. [3, 4]

ProgramName: Japanese (Minor)
Department: School of Modern Languages, Ivan Allen College of Liberal Arts
Description: The School of Modern Languages offers minors in seven languages: Chinese, French, German, Japanese, Korean, Russian, and Spanish. This program is designed for students of all majors who wish to develop their language skills beyond the intermediate level. [4] The language minor demonstrates to future employers and graduate programs a sustained commitment to language and culture studies. [4, 7] Heritage and native speakers are welcome to pursue a language minor (some course restrictions may apply). [4, 7] The School of Modern Languages offers faculty-led study abroad programs in these languages, including our signature Language for Business and Technology (LBAT) summer abroad programs that allow students to complete up to 12 credits toward the 15-credit minor in one semester. [4] Students interested in further advancing their language skills and intercultural competence beyond the minor, are encouraged to consider adding Applied Languages and Intercultural Studies (ALIS) as a double major. [4, 7]

ProgramName: Korean (Minor)

[6, 7] A maximum of 6 credits can be from a list of specified courses including KOR 1001, KOR 1002, KOR 2001, and KOR 2002. [6, 7] Students wishing to pursue the minor should declare it. [17]
Description: The Minor in Korean program is designed for students who wish to develop their language skills to at least an intermediate level and to provide themselves with a greater depth than possible with a certificate program. [11]

ProgramName: Latin American and LatinX Studies (Minor)
Requirements: Students wishing to pursue this minor should declare it by filling out the minor change form with the Student Advisor in Modern Languages. [3] All minors must complete 15 credits, with at least 9 credits at the 3000/4000-level. [3] All courses for the minor must be taken on a letter-grade basis, and a grade of 'C' or better is required in each course. [3] Of the five courses required, three must be SPAN courses. [3]
Description: This interdisciplinary minor connects studies of the regions and peoples in Latin America and the Caribbean, as well as Latino/LatinX populations in the United States, both concurrently in their local and global relationships as well as longitudinally over the course of history. [3, 6] Through the interdisciplinary study of history, politics, economics, literature, media, and languages of these regions and populations, students engage in the comparative study of societies, values, and local/global issues. [3, 6] This minor is designed for undergraduates who will enter a wide range of careers that can lead directly or indirectly to interactions with the people, social organizations, businesses, and governments of Latin America and the Caribbean or with Latino/LatinX communities and related institutions here in the U.S., especially in terms of the critical technological, social, and policy decisions that all those communities face today in a global perspective. [6]
Accredidation: The Georgia Institute of Technology is accredited by the Southern Association of Colleges and Schools Commission on Colleges (SACSCOC) to award baccalaureate, masters, and doctoral degrees. ProgramName: Law, Science, and Technology (Minor)
Requirements: The program is open to all majors and there is no formal application required. To declare the Law, Science, and Technology Minor, current students must submit a Change of Minor form via DocuSign, which requires approval from their academic advisor and the program Co-Director. [6]
Department: School of Public Policy, Ivan Allen College of Liberal Arts
Description: The Law, Science, and Technology minor offers a wide range of curricular opportunities, pre-law advising, and support services for students considering law school and careers in law. [7] The program introduces students to selected areas of law that they are likely to study in law school. [7] Students will begin to develop the skills that they will need to succeed in law school and in law practice. [7] The program welcomes students from every college and major. [7] Some of the courses are taught by full-time faculty, while others are taught by attorneys from the Atlanta area, thereby exposing students to academic and practical perspectives on the practice of law. [7]

ProgramName: Leadership Studies (Minor)
Requirements: To be enrolled in the Leadership Minor program, you must have: Completed 30 credit hours; A cumulative GPA of 2.5 or greater; Completed a formal application to the program and have been admitted to the program.
Department: Scheller College of Business, Institute for Leadership and Social Impact
Concentration: ['Business', 'Global Engineering', 'Public Policy']
Description: The Minor in Leadership Studies provides students with an in-depth knowledge of leadership theory, skills, experience, and application through a rigorous, multi-disciplinary program of study. [2, 5] The minor is comprised of three tracks: Global Engineering, Public Policy and Business, offered through the School of Civil and Environmental Engineering, School of Public Policy and the Institute for Leadership and Social Impact (ILSI) at the Scheller College of Business respectively. [3, 4] Students apply for a specific track, are accepted, and enter the program to begin a prescribed 15 credit hour course of study while satisfying requirements for a bachelor's degree in their major. [3]
ScholarshipAmount: A fellowship of $1800 per semester is available.
ScholarshipType: Merit-based and need-based scholarships are available.

ProgramName: Linguistics (Minor)
Department: The Linguistics Minor is an interdisciplinary minor offered through the School of Modern Languages, which is part of the Ivan Allen College of Liberal Arts.
Description: The School of Modern Languages in partnership with the School of Psychology and School of Interactive Computing offers an undergraduate minor in linguistics (parallel to the certificate, but with one more course). [3] This interdisciplinary minor (15 credit hours total) connects studies of the physical structures and mental processes involved in human language; the psychological and social factors that enable humans to acquire, use, comprehend, and produce language; and the application of computer science to language and technology. [3] A compelling complement to the study of computer science, psychology, or a specific foreign language, the minor is designed for undergraduates who have an interest in theoretical or applied linguistics, culture, psychology, or language technology; and for students who will enter a wide range of careers, such as language education, educational design, language technology, and human/computer interaction. [3]
ScholarshipType: Scholarships at Georgia Tech can be based on academic achievement, athletic ability, geographical location, departmental and community involvement, areas of study, and/or financial need. [19, 34]

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Literature, Media, and Communication
Department: School of Literature, Media, and Communication, Ivan Allen College of Liberal Arts
Fees: In-State: $5,129/Semester, Out-of-State: $16,898/Semester (for 15+ credit hours, based on 2024-2025 academic year rates)

Description: The Bachelor of Science in Literature, Media, and Communication (LMC) offers a vibrant and versatile humanities education in the different modes of representation that structure our technological and global world. [7, 8] Program graduates will have both significant theoretical and hands-on experience with novels, films, games, comic books, web pages, and scientific documents. [8, 10] By learning the modes of communication common to science, technology, and the humanities, LMC graduates are prepared to become leaders at the creative intersections of art, science and technology. [8] The program provides the analytical and technical skills required for a career in fields such as film, the arts, science and technical writing, publicity, and literature. [7, 9]
CostPerCredit: In-State: $427, Out-of-State: $1,407 (based on 2024-2025 academic year rates)

Wayne Clough Georgia Tech Promise Program which provides a debt-free degree for qualifying low-income Georgia residents, and the FIRST Robotics Scholarship of $5,000. [11]
ScholarshipType: Georgia Tech offers merit-based and need-based scholarships, including the HOPE and Zell Miller Scholarships for Georgia residents. [7]

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Materials Science and Engineering
Department: College of Engineering
Concentration: ['Polymer and Fiber materials', 'Structural materials', 'Functional materials', 'Biomaterials']
Description: The materials science and engineering undergraduate program offers a BS degree in Materials Science and Engineering with concentrations in Polymer and Fiber materials, Structural materials, Functional materials, and Biomaterials. [2] This versatile degree combines instruction in the fundamentals of ceramic, metallurgy, and polymer and fiber science and engineering with specialized knowledge and skills, including nano-, bio-, composite, electronic, and optical and magnetic materials. [2] First and second year students study basic chemistry, physics, mathematics, and engineering science and are introduced to the fundamental aspects of materials. [2] Two English courses taken in the freshman year provide the foundation for further instruction in communications that is integrated throughout the curriculum. [2] Third and fourth year students take courses in the engineering and science of materials including the details of materials processing, structure, and properties. [2] The curriculum culminates in a two-course senior design sequence in which students work in teams to design a material, component, or process using previously learned skills and knowledge. [2] Four concentration related courses provide flexibility that allow students in their last two years to focus in a particular area of materials. [2] Five hours of free electives allows students to further specialize or pursue other interests. [2] Courses in the humanities/fine arts and social sciences ensure that graduates appreciate the role of engineering in today's global society. [2] The mission of the Bachelor of Science in Materials Science and Engineering program is to produce graduates well-rounded in the fundamentals of materials science and engineering who are prepared to meet the related needs of industry and government, and prepared for advanced academic study in materials related disciplines. [2] This will be accomplished by providing students with up-to-date knowledge and skills through coursework, modern laboratories, opportunities to conduct cutting edge research with distinguished faculty mentors, and opportunities to participate in leadership and service activities. [2]
Accredidation: The BS in Materials Science and Engineering program is accredited by the Engineering Accreditation Commission(s) of ABET, under the General Criteria and the Program Criteria for Materials, Metallurgical, Ceramics and Similarly Named Engineering Programs. [1]
ScholarshipType: Merit-based, Need-based

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Mathematics
Requirements: General application requirements for first-year students at the Georgia Institute of Technology include the Common Application, the application fee, self-reported high school grades, and ACT/SAT scores. A resume and letters of recommendation are listed as optional and can be submitted if the applicant wishes to do so. [4] Students will develop a strong foundation in quantitative thinking and learn to apply a systems approach to solve real-world problems. [4] The program is flexible, allowing students to customize their degree to align with their specific interests and career aspirations. [4] It prepares graduates for a variety of careers in fields such as academia, business, industry, computer programming, data science, and education, as well as for graduate studies in mathematics and related disciplines. [5] The program also emphasizes undergraduate research opportunities. [4]

ProgramName: Media and Entertainment Studies (Minor)
Description: The School of Literature, Media, and Communication (LMC) sponsors the Film and Media Studies minor, which offers students in any major the opportunity to gain an in-depth knowledge of film and media through concentrated study in courses offered by LMC and the Schools of History and Sociology (HSOC) and Modern Languages (ML). [3] The Film and Media Minor is largely concentrated on the rhetoric, history, theory, and broad cultural context of its subject. [3] While is not aimed at developing skills in film or media production, those interested in gaining background in this area may take a course in video production as part of the minor. [3] The Film and Media Studies minor is comprised of 15 credit hours, of which at least 12 credit hours must be upper-division coursework (numbered 3000 or above). [3]

ProgramName: Middle Eastern and North African Studies (Minor)

[2] This minor is designed for undergraduates who will enter a wide range of careers that can lead directly or indirectly to interactions with the people, the social organizations and businesses, and governments of the Middle East and/or North Africa, both abroad and here in the U.S., especially in terms of the critical technological, social, and policy decisions facing the world today. [2]
ScholarshipType: Scholarships, Grants, Loans, Work-Study

ProgramName: Naval Science (Minor)
Requirements: To apply for the NROTC College Program, a complete application consists of a completed College Program Application, a completed Report of Medical History (dd2807-1), and a completed NROTC AFA Score Sheet. Applicants must also submit a high school or college transcript; students who have been at the host institution for a year do not need to provide high school transcripts. An essay, with a maximum of one page, is required to answer the questions: “What are your top 3 URL communities you wish to commission into and why? If not selected for one of these communities, would you accept your commission?”. A copy of SAT/ACT score reports is also required, as applicable. A letter of admittance is needed if the applicant is not currently enrolled in the university they wish to attend. While not required, letters of recommendation are encouraged. After the application is reviewed, candidates may be invited for an interview. [10]
Department: Ivan Allen College of Liberal Arts
Description: The minor in Naval Science will familiarize railings with basic and advanced concepts of Naval Science with emphasis on naval history, technology, and leadership. The Institute's motto of “Progress and Service” is embodied in military service. This minor will support railings who plan to serve their country by recognizing their academic achievement outside of their major coursework. The minor will also give railings who do not pursue military service a basic working knowledge of the United States Navy and Marine Corps. Concepts learned complement any chosen career path. [2]
ScholarshipAmount: A Naval ROTC scholarship covers the cost of all tuition, fees, and uniforms. Scholarship midshipmen are also paid a subsistence allowance that increases each year. Freshmen receive $250 every month in two bi-weekly payments. Each successive year the allowance increases by $50, sophomores receiving $300, juniors $350, and seniors $400. Scholarship midshipmen also receive $375 each semester for book expenses.
ScholarshipType: NROTC scholarship

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Neuroscience
Requirements: A completed Common Application, a non-refundable application fee, and a high school transcript are required for first-year admission. [11] Applicants can self-report standardized test scores (SAT/ACT) during the application process, with official scores required upon enrollment. [4] While not explicitly required for all applicants, letters of recommendation are considered if submitted, and Georgia Tech will accept up to four. [6]
Department: College of Sciences
Concentration: ['Bachelor of Science in Neuroscience - General', 'Bachelor of Science in Neuroscience - Business Option']
Description: The B.S. in Neuroscience degree at Georgia Tech is an interdisciplinary degree that provides training in behavioral and cognitive, molecular, cellular and systems neuroscience. [3] Students majoring in neuroscience will complete a 120 credit-hour curriculum (plus a required 2-credit class in health). They will learn fundamental principles and up-to-date advances in the field of neuroscience. The program will build on a strong foundation of required courses in the physical sciences and mathematics (chemistry, computer science, calculus, statistics and physics) in order to prepare students with the analytical skills needed to address the complexity of problems in neuroscience. [4] Georgia Tech Neuroscience graduates will possess a command a multiscale understanding of the structure and function of the brain and nervous system, from molecules through cells and networks, to systems and behavior. Each graduate will have knowledge of methods, applied solutions and technologies that enable new discoveries and support their translation into diagnoses and treatments of brain disorders through academic, government and industrial partnerships. [3] The curriculum offers a pre-health option for students who interested in careers in medicine, along with a research option and a business option. [3]
ScholarshipType: Scholarships, Grants, Loans, Work-Study.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Nuclear and Radiological Engineering
Requirements: Georgia Tech utilizes a holistic review process that considers a student's academic background, their potential to contribute to the campus community, and their individual experiences and achievements. Description: The undergraduate curriculum in nuclear and radiological engineering is structured to meet the needs of both the student who contemplates employment immediately after graduation and the student planning to pursue graduate study. It provides maximum flexibility in the form of options for each student to develop their unique interests and capabilities. The core curriculum covers the basic principles of nuclear engineering, nuclear reactor core design, reactor systems engineering, nuclear power economics, reactor operations, radiation sources and detection instruments, radiation transport, radiation protection, criticality safety, regulatory requirements, and radioactive materials management. [8] The program's educational objectives aim for graduates to positively contribute to nuclear and radiological engineering and related fields and to engage in lifelong learning. [8]
Accredidation: The Bachelor of Science in Nuclear and Radiological Engineering (B.S.N.R.E.) program is accredited by the Engineering Accreditation Commission of ABET, under the General Criteria and the Program Criteria for Nuclear, Radiological and Similarly Named Engineering Programs. [12]

Description: The Minor in Philosophy focuses on science and technology. The courses are intended to enable Georgia Tech students to reflect on the nature of their disciplines and to focus their understanding on the context of their lives as professionals and citizens. The Philosophy minor is best for students who wish to concentrate coursework in the field of philosophy. [3]

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Physics
Requirements: General application requirements for first-year admission to Georgia Institute of Technology apply to the Bachelor of Science in Physics. All first-year applicants must submit either the Common Application or the Coalition Application, an application fee, official high school transcripts, and standardized test scores (SAT or ACT). [8] While there is no minimum GPA for first-year applicants, the average GPA for admitted students is high. [3] The program introduces students to selected areas of law that they are likely to study in law school. [3] Students will begin to develop the skills that they will need to succeed in law school and in law practice. [3] Some of the courses are taught by full-time faculty, while others are taught by attorneys from the Atlanta area, thereby exposing students to academic and practical perspectives on the practice of law. [3] The program welcomes students from every college and major. [3] Students majoring in the sciences and engineering may be surprised to learn that their undergraduate background gives them a strong start toward specializations such as intellectual property law, products liability law, and construction law. ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Psychology
Description: The Bachelor of Science in Psychology is a degree program that provides students with a broad-based, research-focused approach to the science of psychology. The curriculum requires courses in mathematics, biology, and chemistry, in addition to a strong foundation in psychology courses. It also emphasizes the development of methodological skills, enabling students to learn the fundamentals of how to ask and answer questions about mental processes and behavior. These skills are designed to be generalizable to many work settings outside of psychology.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Public Policy
Requirements: General application requirements for the Georgia Institute of Technology vary between undergraduate and graduate admissions. All applicants must complete an online application and provide academic transcripts. For graduate programs, a resume and a statement of purpose are generally required, though specific requirements can vary by program. [10, 15] First-year undergraduate applicants must submit either an SAT or ACT score. [11] The writing sections for both the SAT and ACT are not required. [11] While there is no stated minimum GPA for first-year applicants, the admissions process is highly competitive. For transfer students and graduate applicants, minimum GPA requirements may be specified by the individual colleges and programs. [9, 10]
Department: Ivan Allen College of Liberal Arts, Jimmy and Rosalynn Carter School of Public Policy
Concentration: ['Environment and Energy Policy', 'Science and Technology Policy', 'Social and Urban Policy', 'Philosophy', 'Politics and Policy']
Description: The Bachelor of Science in Public Policy (BS PP) provides an education that combines strong analytical skills with an understanding of a range of substantive policy issues and the political, social, and cultural forces that shape public policies. [3] The BS PP core courses provide students with the broad political, economic, and philosophical foundations of thought pertinent to public policy, a base of rigorous quantitative and qualitative analytical approaches, and a solid understanding of the political and social dynamics that structure policy debates and policy outcomes. [3] The curriculum moves from disciplinary foundations (in politics, economics, philosophy, and organization theory) to methods of research and data analysis, and to detailed studies of particular policy problems. [3] Students choose two clusters in environment and energy policy, science and technology policy, social and urban policy, philosophy, or politics and policy, and can select electives in additional areas such as information and telecommunication policy, bioengineering and ethics, and regional development policy. [3] All students have opportunities for internships, research, and study abroad or exchange programs. The BS PP program culminates in a senior-year two-semester capstone "task force" in which students work in teams with outside clients (e.g., Centers for Disease Control, Marcus Autism Center, Multiple Sclerosis Society, Atlanta Food Bank) on actual policy problems. [3] The program's emphasis on the development of problem-solving and analytical skills constitutes a strong comparative advantage for BS PP graduates, many of whom move on to law school, management consulting, public sector policy analysis, or nonprofit management. [3]

Engineering, the sciences, management, architecture, computing, and the liberal arts are impacted by – and affect – the decisions made by governments. The Minor in Public Policy allows students to develop the multidisciplinary thinking skills that are needed for strategic decision making in business and technical professions as well as law and public policy. [10] No matter the major, the minor gives students the tools to understand how policy shapes technology, science, and society. [11] The program is designed to complement both STEM and liberal arts degrees, preparing students to lead, innovate, and make informed decisions. [11] The minor requires 15 credit hours and appears on the official transcript. [11]

It's open to students in all majors. The Women, Science, and Technology (WST) program does what no other gender studies program does: it links science and technology issues to those issues more traditionally associated with women's studies. [3, 4] The WST minor prepares Tech students (women and men majoring in engineering, science, social sciences, and humanities) to live and work in an increasingly diverse world. [3, 4] The minor helps students develop their understanding of the human side of science and engineering involving not only gender issues, but inequalities of race and class as well. [3, 4] WST courses reflect on the theoretical and practical dimensions of diversity. [3, 4] Students are encouraged to explore the values associated with scientific culture and to learn to synthesize knowledge across the disciplines, while viewing science and engineering as social and cultural forces that shape relations among women and men.
